newsitem.title: FRANCE: Convicted French Socialist heads Finance Committee.
newsitem.headline: Convicted French Socialist heads Finance Committee.

text.p: A Socialist parliamentarian twice convicted of illicit party funding activities was on Tuesday named chairman of the French National Assembly's Finance Committee.
Henri Emmanuelli, former leader and treasurer of the French Socialist Party, was elected to the post by the members of the key assembly panel.
He was twice given suspended jail terms after taking political responsibility for the illicit fundraising activities though he denied breaking the law or personally profiting.
Emmanuelli is one of several French political party leaders either convicted or under investigation for involvement in illegal party funding schemes during the 1980s.

The Left, which won power in parliamentary elections earlier this month, won the chairmanship of all six of the assembly's standing committees, with five going to Socialists and one going to a Communist.
Former culture minister Jack Lang took the chairmanship of the Foreign Affairs Committee and former defence minister Paul Quiles will head the defence panel.

Socialist heavyweights Emmanuelli, Lang and Quiles were passed over for the cabinet which Prime Minister Lionel Jospin packed with new, younger ministers, and the committee jobs were seen as intended to soothe disappointment.
Communist Andre Lajoinie, a presidential candidate in 1988, took the chairmanship of the Production Committee.
Socialist ex-communications minister Catherine Tasca was elected chairwoman of the Laws Committee, and Claude Bartolone was picked to head the Cultural Affairs Committee.
Jospin is on Thursday scheduled to make his first policy statement to the newly elected assembly whose speaker is Socialist former prime minister Laurent Fabius.
